conflicts.description: The same human subject entity is named patients in Synthea and person in OMOP, with differing field names such as id/person_id, first/given name, last/family name, and zip/postal code.
conflicts.resolution: Adopted singular, snake_case canonical resources and explicit semantic field names, including person, given_name, family_name, and postal_code.

conflicts.description: Synthea uses encounter terminology while OMOP uses visit occurrence terminology for the same high-level care interaction.
conflicts.resolution: Unified the high-level entity as encounter while retaining OMOP-specific nested visit detail in encounter_detail.

conflicts.description: The provider specialty attribute has spelling and naming differences.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized the verbatim attribute name to specialty_source_value and retained standardized specialty separately.

conflicts.description: Several Synthea columns contain spaces and are not snake_case.
conflicts.resolution: Renamed all target fields to snake_case without changing their semantics.

conflicts.description: Monetary quantities are represented as strings in both sources despite being numeric amounts.
conflicts.resolution: Represented monetary amounts as number and separated ambiguous Synthea base or line-item amounts from OMOP's explicitly classified charge, cost, and paid amounts.

conflicts.description: Counts are represented as strings in source schemas.
conflicts.resolution: Canonical count fields use integer.

conflicts.description: Synthea declares the value datatype indicator as number and stores all result values as string, while OMOP separates numeric, string, and concept-valued results.
conflicts.resolution: Used typed, atomic result columns and retained a verbatim source value; numeric conversion is represented only in numeric value fields.

conflicts.description: Several OMOP columns have source types inconsistent with their descriptions, including categorical invalidation reasons typed as date, a vocabulary name typed as integer, prescription text typed as integer, and birth components typed as date.
conflicts.resolution: Corrected these to string or integer according to their stated semantics.

conflicts.description: Fields described as containing date and time are typed as date in the source schemas.
conflicts.resolution: Canonical event timestamps use datetime.

conflicts.description: The Synthea encounter provider column is documented as an organization foreign key, whereas OMOP provider_id identifies a clinician and care_site_id identifies a facility.
conflicts.resolution: Mapped the Synthea attribute to canonical care_site_id and kept clinician provider_id semantically separate.

conflicts.description: Synthea stores source vocabulary codes directly, while OMOP distinguishes standardized concept identifiers from verbatim source codes.
conflicts.resolution: Kept source_code, source_concept_id, and standardized concept_id fields distinct across clinical domains.

conflicts.description: Source unit strings and standardized unit concepts are different representations, and source units may not be SI.
conflicts.resolution: Retained verbatim unit_source_value separately from unit_concept_id and specified normalized numeric values should use the standardized, preferably SI, unit.

conflicts.description: The term cost is semantically ambiguous in Synthea, while OMOP differentiates charges, provider costs, and payments.
conflicts.resolution: Preserved Synthea values as base_or_line_item_amount and maintained OMOP financial categories as separate attributes.

conflicts.description: Synthea uses compact source encodings such as M/F while OMOP distinguishes source values from standardized concepts.
conflicts.resolution: Retained source encodings in gender_source_value and kept standardized concept identifiers separate.

conflicts.description: Synthea repeats address attributes in entity tables, while OMOP normalizes geographic data into location.
conflicts.resolution: Adopted a normalized location resource and linked persons and care sites through foreign keys; Synthea-derived location identifiers are generated where needed.

conflicts.description: Synthea combines laboratory measurements and other observations in one table, whereas OMOP separates them by clinical domain.
conflicts.resolution: Retained separate measurement and observation resources so numeric measurements and non-measurement clinical assertions remain semantically homogeneous.

conflicts.description: Synthea has one encounter level, while OMOP supports a parent visit plus nested visit details.
conflicts.resolution: Used encounter for the high-level visit and encounter_detail as a normalized child resource.

conflicts.description: Synthea embeds event descriptions while OMOP generally resolves standardized names through concept references.
conflicts.resolution: Preserved source event descriptions and separately retained normalized vocabulary concepts rather than conflating event text with concept master data.

conflicts.description: Synthea contains explicit domain tables without exact one-to-one OMOP counterparts in the supplied schema.
conflicts.resolution: Retained these as independent normalized target resources instead of forcing them into semantically broader OMOP tables.

conflicts.description: A Synthea encounter is a single record, while an OMOP visit occurrence may have one-to-many visit-detail children and nested detail relationships.
conflicts.resolution: Modeled one encounter to many encounter_detail records, with optional self-references for parent and preceding details.

conflicts.description: Synthea embeds one current address per person record, while OMOP allows a normalized location to be referenced by many persons or organizations.
conflicts.resolution: Modeled location as a reusable parent entity referenced by person and care_site.

conflicts.description: Cohort membership is polymorphic: a cohort can contain persons, providers, or visits, and each subject can belong to many cohorts and periods.
conflicts.resolution: Retained cohort membership as an associative resource keyed by definition, subject, and start date, with subject domain declared by the cohort definition.

conflicts.description: Concepts participate in many-to-many directional relationships.
conflicts.resolution: Retained an explicit concept_relationship bridge with source concept, target concept, and relationship type as its composite key.

conflicts.description: Equivalent person entities use differently named source primary keys.
conflicts.resolution: Unified them under person.person_id and included both source primary keys in provenance.

conflicts.description: Equivalent encounter entities use differently named primary keys.
conflicts.resolution: Unified them under encounter.encounter_id and included both source identifiers in provenance.

conflicts.description: Multiple Synthea event tables declare no primary key, whereas OMOP supplies event identifiers, though some are not formally declared as source primary keys.
conflicts.resolution: Canonical event resources use required identifiers; OMOP identifiers are preserved where present and synthetic identifiers are generated only for source rows without explicit event identifiers.

conflicts.description: Synthea describes foreign-key semantics but declares no foreignKeys, while OMOP explicitly declares most relationships.
conflicts.resolution: Declared canonical foreign keys for persons, encounters, providers, care sites, concepts, and normalized child resources.

conflicts.description: Several OMOP associative or definition tables lack declared primary keys despite having identifiable natural or documented unique keys.
conflicts.resolution: Introduced composite keys for cohort membership and concept relationships and a documented identifier key for cohort definitions.
